statements.text: The Prime Minister said President Trump announced a reciprocal energy ceasefire, and that President Zelenskyy assured him Ukraine would implement it immediately once a start date is confirmed. He said he will discuss this further with President Zelenskyy in the coming days.

The Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military aid and fiscal packages to provide urgent support in the coming weeks, and is to tell President Zelenskyy so when they meet.

The Prime Minister said the UK assesses that the incident at RAF Fairford is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard. He said the UK will not tolerate these threats, will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks, and will bring further sanctions against Iran and the IRGC.

The Prime Minister said he raised the Falkland Islands and the islanders' declared will to remain British with President Trump, and that he will emphasise this in his UN General Assembly speech and will always do whatever it takes to uphold it.

The Prime Minister confirmed the UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. He said it is in Britain's interest to secure a deal and that he will work hard over the next 5 weeks to achieve it.

The Prime Minister said a food and drink trade deal at the UK-EU summit would add the equivalent of over 10 billion pounds per year to the UK economy by 2040, lifting a burden that can reach 1,400 pounds on a single shipment and removing export health certificates costing up to 200 pounds each time. He said the proposed energy deal could cut wholesale energy costs in Northern Ireland by 20%.

The UK is delivering £45 million of surface-to-air missiles to Ukraine and standing by plans to fully implement a maritime services ban on Russian LNG exports. The UK will accelerate deliveries of British Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which have committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5000 to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of the package for Ukraine's most urgent winter needs.

At their meeting, the leaders said Russia had no interest in peace. The Prime Minister said the UK would continue to develop innovative military solutions for use on the battlefield in Ukraine, and would continue its diplomatic efforts to support international supplies of defensive equipment.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey urged partners to back the ban on Russian LNG, as the UK has done, to curtail the war chest funding Putin, and will do so at the IMF meetings in Bangkok.

The Prime Minister said the UK has announced new funding to help Ukraine through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package that brings over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity under UK sanctions.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK's support for Ukraine is vital for keeping the UK safe, that the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes, and that Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

The Prime Minister confirmed Britain's decision to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling, and confirmed the Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions. He condemned the appalling attacks on King Khalid International Airport.

The Prime Minister told the Commons the UK will meet its NATO commitments in full, that he and Chancellor Merz agreed a new partnership in Berlin to tackle Russian hybrid threats, and confirmed a new National Centre for Information Defence.

Andy Burnham said he made an offer to the Scottish Government to work together on spreading opportunities across Scotland's regions. Douglas Alexander said the offer is genuine and the Scotland Office is ready to work alongside the Scottish Government to make it happen.

Andy Burnham's speech offers Scotland DWP devolution, a localised employment support model shaped by Holyrood. He said the National Economic Council will meet with the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in a couple of weeks to put the offer on the table.

The site of Great British Railways' headquarters at Becketwell in Derby was unveiled. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029. The HQ is estimated to bring a £151 million boost to Derby and will accommodate up to 450 GBR staff.

Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, that she is delighted Becketwell will become GBR's new home, and that with 600 apprenticeships opening up the government is investing in the people who will build the railway.

Pat McFadden said the government is determined to build a strong pipeline of skilled workers, and that the foundation apprenticeship forms part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities to earn or learn.
The King has appointed William James Baxter QPM DL as Lord-Lieutenant of County Tyrone, succeeding Sir Robert Scott, who retired on 17 June 2026.
The Prime Minister confirmed that during the UK's G20 presidency in 2027, AI will be placed centre stage, with the aim of agreeing a single set of global principles and standards on AI.
